description: Chucktown Floods: Adapting to Flooding in Charleston is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by College of Charleston; South Carolina Sea Grant; Charleston Resilience Network. The Chucktown Floods site gives municipalities, stakeholders in business and industry, and individual homeowners a way to findresilience tools and data relevant to flooding in the Charleston County area. The mobile-friendly site serves Charleston County residents, businesses, and municipalities. Coverage: Charleston County, South Carolina. The toolkit lists hazards: Erosion and Shoreline Recession, Flooding – Coastal. Assets: Aquatic and Marine Resources, Critical Facilities, Cultural and Community Services, Natural Areas and Wildlife, Property. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
